content.text: {"predictors": [{"name": "Inventory Growth Divergence", "construction": "For each fiscal year, compute the growth rate of inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus the growth rate of sales (item SALE), both year-over-year. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June after the reporting lag. Restrict to firms carrying meaningful inventory (exclude financials and pure service firms).", "rationale": "Inventory building faster than sales signals demand overestimation and future markdowns, while lean inventory relative to sales signals efficient operations and hidden demand strength.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (inventory growth well below sales growth)"}, {"name": "Accrued Working Capital Intensity", "construction": "Compute the annual change in non-cash working capital = change in (current assets - cash) minus change in (current liabilities - short-term debt), scaled by average total assets, using Compustat items ACT, CHE, LCT, DLC, AT. Rank each June.", "rationale": "Large non-cash working-capital accruals reflect low-quality earnings that revert, so firms bloating working capital tend to underperform relative to those generating cash-backed earnings.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "Capital Expenditure Acceleration", "construction": "Compute the ratio of current-year capital expenditures (Compustat CAPX) to the three-year prior average of CAPX, then subtract the industry-median of this ratio. Rank each June after reporting lag.", "rationale": "Firms sharply accelerating investment tend to overinvest at cyclical peaks and subsequently disappoint, consistent with q-theory and empire-building frictions.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "Gross Margin Trend Stability", "construction": "Using quarterly Compustat, compute gross margin = (SALEQ - COGSQ)/SALEQ for the last 8 quarters, then take the slope of a linear trend divided by the standard deviation of the quarterly margins. Rank cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "A steadily rising, low-volatility gross margin signals durable competitive positioning that the market underappreciates, while deteriorating margins forecast earnings shortfalls.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Trading Volume Trend Decay", "construction": "For each stock, compute average daily share turnover (CRSP volume divided by shares outstanding) over the most recent 3 months minus average turnover over months 4 through 12. Rank monthly.", "rationale": "Declining relative turnover reflects fading investor attention and neglect, and neglected stocks earn a premium as attention eventually re-normalizes.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (declining turnover)"}, {"name": "Return Convexity to Market", "construction": "Regress a stock's monthly excess returns on market excess returns and squared market excess returns over trailing 60 months. Rank stocks by the coefficient on the squared term (coskewness proxy).", "rationale": "Stocks whose returns are convex in the market provide crash protection that investors overpay for, so low-convexity stocks command higher expected returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the convexity coefficient"}, {"name": "Debt Maturity Concentration", "construction": "Compute the fraction of total debt maturing within one year = DLC / (DLC + DLTT) from Compustat. Rank each June, controlling for leverage quintile.", "rationale": "High reliance on short-term debt exposes firms to rollover and refinancing risk that is not fully priced, commanding a risk premium.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Dividend Initiation Persistence Gap", "construction": "Identify firms that have paid dividends (CRSP distribution codes) for at least 3 consecutive years but whose payout ratio (dividends/earnings) declined in the most recent year while earnings rose. Flag this divergence as a binary/continuous signal.", "rationale": "Managers holding payout flat while earnings grow are conservatively signaling and building slack, and such quietly strengthening firms are underpriced relative to full-payout peers.", "higher_returns_for": "firms with rising retained earnings and lagging payout"}, {"name": "Idiosyncratic Volatility Compression", "construction": "Estimate idiosyncratic volatility as the standard deviation of residuals from a market-model regression over the trailing 12 months, and separately over the prior 12 months. Compute the ratio (recent/prior). Rank monthly.", "rationale": "A sharp compression in idiosyncratic volatility signals resolution of firm-specific uncertainty and stabilizing fundamentals that the market prices with delay.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the ratio (volatility falling)"}, {"name": "Analyst Coverage Scaled by Size", "construction": "Compute the number of I/B/E/S analysts issuing FY1 estimates divided by the log of market capitalization (CRSP price times shares). Rank cross-sectionally each month.", "rationale": "Low coverage relative to firm size indicates neglect and weaker information flow, and such under-followed stocks earn a premium as information asymmetry resolves.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (under-covered for their size)"}]}
